summary: The ladder starts with September's gross revenue against August, shows that every store fell, and traces the fall to two causes: a chain-wide drop in orders from mid-September as customers visited less often, and a smaller average order as fewer jaffles were sold; it then sizes the levers by store, by customer visits and by jaffle product.

narration.text: September 2026 gross revenue was $208.0K, down 13.4% from $240.4K in August.
Every store fell against August, with Brooklyn down 14.9% to $93.0K, Philadelphia down 14.7% and Chicago the smallest drop at 8.0%.
Set against the run of complete months, September ended a steep climb from July's $200.7K to August's $240.4K, and October held level at $208.6K.
September was still 108.5% above the same month last year, so this is a step back from an unusually strong August rather than a collapse.
The drop came mainly from fewer orders, which fell 9.1% to 19,345, after weekly orders stepped down from 4,948 in the week of 7 September to 4,029 the week after and stayed lower.
The average order also shrank, down 4.8% to $10.75, while customers rose to 1,613.
The basket shrank because jaffle units fell 20.5% to 6,122 while beverage units fell only 8.8% to 22,163.

Win back the weekly run rate store by store, starting with Brooklyn, where weekly orders fell from 2,331 in the week of 7 September to 1,891 the week after and were still 1,861 in the week of 5 October.
Bring regular customers back more often, since orders per customer fell from 14.3 to 12.8 at Brooklyn and from 13.7 to 11.1 at Chicago even as customer counts held or grew.
Test restoring jaffle attachment on the weakest lines, such as nutellaphone who dis?, where units fell 26.3% to 1,188, to lift an average order that has slipped to $10.75.

digests.question: What should we do?
digests.headline: win back orders, visits, jaffles
digests.summary: September 2026 gross revenue was $208.0K, down 13.4% from August's $240.4K, with every store lower and October holding level. The drop came from a mid-September step down in orders, fewer visits per customer and a weaker jaffle attach, so the levers are winning back weekly orders store by store, bringing regulars back more often and restoring jaffle sales.
